item.text: {"text":"Search results did not identify a verified 2024–2026 NextItNet study matching a lightweight title/description encoder trained entirely from scratch. Related work supports semantic–collaborative alignment: [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183) uses fine-grained semantic codes, cross-attention fusion and masked alignment objectives; [ST2SI (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171.pdf) highlights limitations of coarse sentence-level representations and aligns item text with IDs. These provide design motivation, not evidence that a randomly initialized text encoder improves NextItNet under the specified budget. Their LLM-based components are unsuitable for direct adoption under the no-pretrained-weights constraint.\n\nA plausible experiment—not an established result—is to retain [NextItNet’s residual dilated-convolution backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) and jointly train a small token-embedding encoder with masked mean pooling or a short text CNN. Fuse title/description features with item IDs through a learned residual gate; optionally add a low-weight item-ID/text contrastive loss within the same network. Missing text should produce zero semantic contribution, preserving the ID representation. Compare against an otherwise matched ID-only control; separately ablate titles, descriptions and alignment loss using macro validation HR@10. Token-level features could distinguish names, editions or model numbers, but improvement remains uncertain with sparse supervision. Text similarity alone does not establish product compatibility or unmet need. Keep one jointly trained checkpoint per category and identical feature construction during training and prediction."}
